blocks.title: Instantaneous and average rate
blocks.text: The rate at any one instant during an interval is the instantaneous rate. The average rate of reaction is the rate between two specific times, the rate over a time period.
The average and instantaneous rates are equal at only one instant in any interval: at first the instantaneous rate is higher than the average, and at the end of the interval it is lower.

blocks.caption: Sample Problem 7.1: ammonia in the Haber process, N2 + 3H2 gives 2NH3
rows: delta C / delta t = 2.7 mol dm-3 / 1 min
Average rate between 1.0 and 4.0 min, [NH3] 3.5 then 6.2 mol dm-3

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The instantaneous rate cannot be found this way: 2.7 mol dm-3 is the change between 1.0 and 4.0 min, and dividing it by 1 min gives neither the instantaneous nor the average rate. The instantaneous rate at 1.0 min needs the slope of the tangent to the concentration-time curve at 1.0 min, which the book does not give.
